title: What shape do two equal crossing strips make at sixty degrees?
description: Two equal strips cut each other in half and cross at sixty degrees. Angles in two isosceles triangles give every angle of the shape, and Keeko then doubts that equal angles must mean a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal diagonals that cut each other in half always give four right angles and equal opposite sides, so the shape is a rectangle. Watch for students who think four equal angles must mean four equal sides.

source: Two equal diagonals bisect each other and meet at 60°. Find
video_script.why: The child sees why equal diagonals that cut each other in half always give a rectangle, by finding every angle once for a sixty degree crossing.
video_script.substitution: Find the angles at O, then the base angles of two isosceles triangles, add one of each at every corner, and match triangles for the opposite sides.
video_script.anchor: quadrilateral ABCD whose equal diagonals AC and BD cross at O with 60 degrees between them
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the shape must be a square because all four angles are equal; but side AD faces the 120 degree angle and is longer than side AB.
video_script.payoff_line: Every corner is ninety degrees and the shape is a rectangle

final_answer.spoken: every corner is ninety degrees and the shape is a rectangle

maths_rules: AC = BD and O is the midpoint of both, so OA = OB = OC = OD
angle AOB = angle COD = 60 degrees (vertically opposite); angle AOD = angle BOC = 180 - 60 = 120 degrees (linear pair)
triangle AOB with OA = OB: base angles add to 180 - 60 = 120, so each is 120 / 2 = 60 degrees
triangle AOD with OA = OD: base angles add to 180 - 120 = 60, so each is 60 / 2 = 30 degrees
each corner is 60 + 30 = 90 degrees, so all four angles are 90 degrees
SAS: triangle AOB is congruent to triangle COD and triangle AOD is congruent to triangle COB, so AB = CD and AD = CB
triangle AOB has three 60 degree angles, so AB = OA; AD faces the 120 degree angle, so AD > OA = AB; the shape is not a square
video_script.design: One idea: equal diagonals that bisect each other make a rectangle. Wrong idea: all four angles equal means a square. The figure with O and the sixty degree angle stays on the board.

<bookmark mark='sides'/>Matching sides give eigh B equals C D, and eigh D equals C B.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
<bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it must be a square, because all four angles are the same.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>Four right angles only make a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='long'/>Side eigh D faces the big angle, so it is longer than side eigh B.
<bookmark mark='end'/>The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.
